rows.label: Concept
rows.text: A **prism** is a transparent element with two non-parallel refracting faces (triangular or right-angled types), whose **angle A** is the angle between them (NEB 2021). The deviation it produces, δ = i + e − A, traces a **U-shaped curve** with the angle of incidence, dipping to a single **minimum deviation δm** (NEB 2024, 2m).…

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Symmetry = minimum:** i = e is the condition at δm, not a general identity.  ·  **The i–δ curve is U-shaped** — every other angle of incidence gives a larger deviation.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Reasoning (2m): Why is the deviation at minimum independent of small errors in i?** — Near the minimum the δ(i) curve is flat (slope zero), so small changes in i hardly change δ — measurements are most accurate there.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: The 2020 4m derivation is the classic — reversibility + symmetry + r₁ + r₂ = A.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **Reversibility proves symmetry:** retracing the emergent ray must retrace the incident one, forcing i = e at the minimum.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: At δm: i = e, r₁ = r₂ = A/2, ray parallel to base.  ·  Single minimum: δ(i) symmetric about the symmetric path.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Red light has a smaller δm than violet in the same prism — the seed of dispersion.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Prism's Sweet Spot Turn a prism slowly and the emerging ray swings — the deviation shrinks, reaches a lowest value, then grows again. That lowest value, the **minimum deviation**, happens when the ray passes symmetrically, and it is the key to measuring refractive index in the spectrometer.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 What is a prism? (NEB 2021) A **prism** is a transparent refracting element with two plane refracting faces that are **not parallel**. **Two types:** triangular prism (spectrometers, dispersion) and right-angled (totally reflecting) prism (periscopes, binoculars).…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 75:** δm feeds directly into the prism formula n = sin((A+δm)/2)/sin(A/2). - **To Topic 76:** for small A, δm ≈ (n − 1)A. - **To dispersion:** n depends on colour, so δm does too — violet bends more than red.
